transcript.content: Hello, welcome in. I'm Dr. [Name]. To start, can you tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Um, yeah… I came in because I feel like I just can’t get things organized. Like, I’m trying to keep up with schoolwork, and I also have this little accessories shop thing, and somehow everything ends up in piles—supplies, receipts, due dates, assignment notes.

And then I’ll be like, “Okay, I should start with this,” but then I see something else I forgot, or I remember I needed to write something down, and then it’s just… I don’t know what to do first. Even my desk looks like a craft store exploded, which is kind of funny but also not, because then I miss stuff or lose track of what I’m supposed to be doing.
Thinking back, did you notice this kind of trouble organizing tasks and staying focused as far back as childhood or your school years, or did it start more recently?

Yeah, it definitely goes back. My mom actually still has these little notes from elementary school teachers—she keeps everything, like she has boxes of old school stuff and drawings I did that are honestly kind of embarrassing—but the notes would say I was out of my seat a lot, or talking before I was called on.

And I remember… well, she tells me more than I remember, but I’d rush through group activities, even if I understood what we were supposed to do. Like I just wanted to get to the next thing or blurt out the answer. So I don’t think it’s brand new.
Do you still notice yourself feeling restless, needing to move around, or blurting things out/interrupting others in your day-to-day life now, as an adult?

Yeah, I do. Like even if I’m just sitting there and I’m not going anywhere, it feels like my body is kind of… buzzing? Like I need to move, or shift around, or do something with my hands.

It’s worse when I’m supposed to just sit still and listen, like in class or when someone’s explaining something for a while. I’ll be trying to pay attention, but my body feels like it’s already trying to leave, if that makes sense.
Would you say these organization and focus problems cause real difficulties in more than one area of your life—for example, both at school and in running your shop—rather than just one?

Yeah… it’s not just one place. I wish it was, because then I could be like, okay, it’s just my room or just the shop stuff, but it’s kind of spilling everywhere.

With school, I missed some required steps for my program—like forms or whatever I was supposed to do in order—and now my financial aid is kind of at risk, which is really stressing me out. And then with my shop, when I’m doing projects with other people, I can tell they don’t rely on me the same way now. Like they’ll take over parts or not ask me to handle certain things, because I’ve dropped the ball before.

It’s embarrassing, honestly, because I’m not trying to be flaky. I’ll have good intentions and then everything gets messy and suddenly something important got missed.
Have these focus and organization difficulties been fairly constant over time, or do they come and go in distinct periods, like during times when your mood or energy is unusually high or low?

It’s been pretty constant, I think. Like, not exactly every single day the same level, but it’s not only when my mood is a certain way or anything.

The really noticeable problems have been going on for, um… about two years now—two years and a couple months, I guess. It started getting bad after I changed schools and suddenly had to manage the business program stuff and my accessories shop with way less structure. Before that there were signs, but that’s when it became like, “Okay, I’m actually not keeping up.”
Have you noticed these focus and restlessness problems happening even during times when you weren't feeling anxious, worried, or using any substances like caffeine, cannabis, or other drugs?

Um… I’m not totally sure, honestly. I haven’t really tracked it that way, like “today I had caffeine” or “today I was anxious” and compared it.

I mean, I know there are days where I’m not especially worried about anything and I still feel kind of all over the place, but I don’t know if I can say for sure what was happening with caffeine or anything else every time. I drink stuff without thinking sometimes, like I’ll have a coffee and then forget I even had it, which probably doesn’t help me answer this very clearly.

So… I guess I’d say I’ve noticed it enough that it doesn’t feel only tied to being anxious, but I’m not sure how to separate all of that out.

Have you ever had distinct periods lasting several days or more where you felt unusually high, elated, or full of energy, needed much less sleep than usual, or had racing thoughts, separate from your usual day-to-day restlessness?

I don’t think so? I mean, I have days where I’m really wired, but it’s hard for me to tell what’s “unusually” high versus just me being me.

Like sometimes I’ll get super into an idea for the shop and I’ll stay up later than I should looking at beads or packaging stuff, and then suddenly I’m on some totally different website looking at shelves or, I don’t know, room setups. But that’s not really like several days of being elated or anything… at least I don’t think so.

The sleep thing is hard too, because I already mess up my sleep sometimes, but I wouldn’t say I’m walking around needing way less sleep and feeling amazing for days. I guess I haven’t noticed a clear separate period like that.

final_diagnosis.reason: Patient reports chronic, longstanding difficulties with disorganization, distractibility, forgetfulness, and impulsivity (blurting answers, interrupting) alongside physical restlessness and an internal sense of needing to move, with onset clearly documented in childhood (teacher notes, corroborated by mother). Symptoms are pervasive across two settings (school and business), cause functional impairment (financial aid risk, loss of trust from business partners), and have been persistent/constant for over 6 months (in fact lifelong, with clear worsening 2+ years ago under increased demands). Symptoms are not confined to episodes of mood elevation/depression (no distinct manic/hypomanic periods identified) and are not better explained solely by anxiety or substance use, though these were not perfectly ruled out. The combination of inattentive and hyperactive-impulsive symptoms since childhood with adult persistence supports ADHD, Combined Type.
